newsitem.title: DENMARK: Virgin mulls new complaint on SAS price cuts.
newsitem.headline: Virgin mulls new complaint on SAS price cuts.

text.p: Cut-price airline Virgin Express said on Friday it might complain anew to EU transport authorities over what it sees as unfair price cuts by Scandinavian Airline System (SAS).
"SAS is attempting to target us. They are doing everything thay can to discourage competition. I think that I shall send a new letter," managing director Jonathan Ornstein told Reuters.

Ornstein said SAS was offering below-cost fares on its routes competing with his Brussels-based airline's European flights from Copenhagen. Virgin on Friday increased its daily Copenhagen-Brussels departures to two from one previously.
"I have no problem about competition but I find it problematic that an airline dumps prices to eliminate competition," Ornstein said.
Virgin wrote to European Union transport officials in September complaining that its new budget-fare daily service from Copenhagen to Brussels was the victim of foul play by SAS.

It said that SAS cut the price of its own flights in a similar time slot but left fares on other departures for the Belgian capital unchanged. Virgin's British owner Richard Branson then notified EU authorities of the situation and threatened formal action if the problem was not solved.
On November 5, SAS announced it trimmed all its fares on the route, warding off a formal complaint for selective price cutting to the EU by Virgin.

Denmark's Den Danske Bank forecast in a report this month that higher fuel costs could knock 30 percent off SAS' nine-month 1996 result due on November 19, downgrading the troubled airline's shares and earnings estimates.
Analysts do not expect SAS' nine-month result to match the 1.01 billion Swedish crowns earned in 1996's third quarter.
The airline is currently being hit by escalating competition on its key European and Nordic routes.
Aviation insiders say British Airways, which signed a franchise deal with Denmark's Sun-Air in May, appears to be positioning for a major assault on SAS.
The Norwegian carrier Braathens SAFE this month launched six daily flights between Stockholm and Oslo and plans to expand flights on Transwede, a domestic airline it half owns.

Virgin Express' Ornstein said his airline could consider launching services linking the three Nordic capitals, Oslo, Copenhagen and Sweden next year, when its fleet capacity was expected to be doubled. --Soeren Linding Jakobsen, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
